sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary**
TCS reported a 6.0% growth in revenue from operations to ₹255,324 crore in FY 2025, driven by a strong and resilient order book despite increased macroeconomic uncertainty. The company's EBIT margin stood at 24.3% in FY 2025, a 30-basis point decline from the previous year, influenced by headwinds from merit-based interventions and investments in infrastructure and capability building. However, tailwinds such as improved utilization, productivity, and realization, along with favorable currency movements, contributed positively to the margins. The constant currency revenue growth for the year was 4.2%, with business growth contributing 4.2% and impact of exchange rate contributing 1.8%.

**Investment Thesis**
Our investment thesis for TCS is based on the company's ability to navigate the challenging global economic environment and deliver resilient growth. With a strong order book and a diversified revenue stream across industry verticals, including Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (37.0% of revenue), Communication, Media and Technology (18.0%), and Consumer Business (15.7%), TCS is well-positioned to capitalize on opportunities for growth. The company's focus on continuous transformation, innovation-driven growth, and proactive policy responses will help mitigate the risks associated with financial market volatility, demographic shifts, and fiscal constraints. With a robust investment strategy and a total funds invested of ₹47,222 crore, TCS is expected to deliver long-term value to shareholders. We believe that TCS's strong financial performance, combined with its ability to adapt to changing market dynamics, makes it an attractive investment opportunity.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body: TCS is an IT services, consulting, and business solutions organization that has been partnering with many of the world’s largest businesses in their transformational journeys for the last 57 years. The Company offers a comprehensive portfolio of services and offerings, including application development and management, digital transformation, AI, data and cloud services, engineering services, cognitive business operations, cyber security, and products & platforms. TCS considers industry verticals as its primary go-to-market business segments, with the five key vertical clusters being Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI), Communication, Media and Technology (CMT), Consumer Business, Life Sciences and Healthcare, Manufacturing, and Others. For the year ended March 31, 2025, the Company reported revenue from operations of ₹255.32 billion, with segment-wise revenue being ₹94.60 billion for BFSI, ₹25.17 billion for Manufacturing, ₹40.20 billion for Consumer Business, ₹45.89 billion for CMT, ₹26.46 billion for Life Sciences and Healthcare, and ₹23.01 billion for Others.

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body: <section prose>The financial performance of TCS is highlighted by a 6.0% growth in revenue from operations, reaching ₹255,324 crore in FY 2025, compared to ₹240,893 crore in FY 2024. The profit after tax attributable to shareholders of the Company stood at ₹48,553 crore in FY 2025, representing a 4.2% increase from ₹46,585 crore in the previous year. Earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) were ₹62,165 crore, with an EBIT margin of 24.3%. The constant currency revenue growth for FY 2025 was 4.2%, after adjusting for the positive impact of 1.8% from currency movements. The Company's basic and diluted earnings per share were ₹134.19 for FY 2025, up from ₹127.74 in the previous year.</section>

sections.title: Balance Sheet Health + Cash Flow
sections.body:
The balance sheet of TCS exhibits a healthy position, with a substantial amount of cash and cash equivalents of ₹8,342 crore as of March 31, 2025. The company's total carrying value of financial assets stands at ₹1,11,109 crore, comprising cash and cash equivalents, bank deposits, investments, and other financial assets. On the liabilities side, the total carrying value of financial liabilities is ₹32,523 crore, consisting of trade payables, lease liabilities, and other financial liabilities. The company's other financial liabilities have decreased from ₹9,065 crore to ₹8,542 crore (current) and from ₹365 crore to ₹680 crore (non-current) over the past year, indicating a relatively stable debt position.

In terms of cash flow, the company's ability to generate cash from operations is evident from its profit before tax of ₹65,331 crore for the year ended March 31, 2025. The depreciation and amortisation expense of ₹5,242 crore and significant non-cash items of ₹128 crore (allocable) and ₹7 crore (unallocable) are notable. However, without explicit cash flow statement data, a comprehensive analysis of the company's cash flow position is not possible. Nonetheless, the company's revenue from operations of ₹2,55,324 crore and profit for the year of ₹48,797 crore suggest a robust financial performance. A detailed cash flow analysis would require additional data, which is not provided in the given excerpts.

sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of TCS has provided a comprehensive overview of the company's performance and outlook amidst a challenging global economic environment. As stated in the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, the world GDP grew at a steady rate of 3.3% in 2024, but is expected to decline to 2.8% in 2025 and 3% in 2026. Despite these headwinds, TCS remains confident in its ability to navigate the challenges and capitalize on opportunities. The company's investment strategy focuses on selecting a balanced mix of long-term and short-term instruments, with total funds invested standing at ₹47,222 crore in FY 2025, comprising investments in mutual funds, government securities, and others (₹30,956 crore), deposits with banks (₹12,831 crore), and cash and bank balances (₹3,435 crore).

The management has identified key demand drivers expected to power the company's growth in FY 2026, including technology modernization and transformation, business transformation, operating model transformation, and tech-enabled sustainability. Segment-wise, the company reported revenue growth across various industry verticals, with Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) contributing ₹94,597 crore in revenue, followed by Communication, Media, and Technology (₹45,893 crore), Consumer Business (₹40,197 crore), Life Sciences and Healthcare (₹26,456 crore), Manufacturing (₹25,170 crore), and Others (₹23,011 crore). The management's focus on driving sustainable growth, fostering innovation, and delivering value to clients, employees, and shareholders is expected to enable the company to stay resilient and adapt to the changing market dynamics.

sections.title: Key Risks
sections.body:
The key risks associated with TCS are multifaceted and can be categorized into several areas. Firstly, the company faces risks related to intellectual property (IP) infringement and leakage, which may lead to potential liabilities, increased litigation, and reputation impact. Additionally, litigation risks may arise from commercial disputes, alleged violation of intellectual property rights, personal data breaches, and employment-related matters. These risks can result in substantial financial implications, reputation damage, and legal expenses. To mitigate these risks, TCS has established an industry-leading IP management framework, contractual and operational controls, and a well-defined software asset lifecycle governance framework.

Furthermore, TCS is exposed to sustainability risks, including climate change and environmental aspects, which can affect its growth, profitability, and reputation. The company faces physical risks to life and property due to extreme weather events, transition risks resulting from disruptions in the market and emerging regulations, and risks of non-compliance with regulatory requirements. However, TCS also sees opportunities in the growing commitment by enterprises to reduce their carbon footprint and regulatory requirements, which can open up new avenues for providing business-led technology solutions. Other key risks include technology disruption, which can happen at an unprecedented pace, and the potential impact of disruptive technologies on TCS' business model and operations. The company's robust risk management initiatives, commitment to innovation and excellence, and proactive approach to mitigating these risks are expected to enable TCS to navigate the challenges of the IT industry and global environment.

sections.title: Recent Developments
sections.body:
The recent developments at TCS reflect the company's resilience and adaptability in a rapidly changing technology environment. In FY 2025, TCS achieved a year-over-year revenue growth of 6.0%, demonstrating a strong business performance amidst uncertainty. On a constant currency basis, revenue grew by 4.2%, outpacing the growth in FY 2024. The company's operating margin stood at 24.3% in FY 2025, a marginal decline of 30 basis points compared to FY 2024, primarily due to the impact of annual wage hikes and strategic investments. However, cost pressures were partially offset by improvements in workforce utilization, productivity, and realization, along with favourable currency movements.

TCS' financial performance is a testament to its robust business model, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.2% over the past five financial years. The company's revenue has consistently grown, from ₹164,177 crore in FY 2021 to ₹255,324 crore in FY 2025. Operating profit has also increased, from ₹42,481 crore in FY 2021 to ₹62,165 crore in FY 2025. With a strong balance sheet, zero debt, and consistently high shareholder returns, TCS is well-positioned to navigate economic downturns and invest in new capabilities, research, and innovation. The company's focus on operational excellence, cost optimization, and prudent use of working capital has resulted in robust cash conversion and increased invested funds, further strengthening its return ratios.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The bull case for TCS is supported by the company's strong and resilient order book, with revenue from operations growing 6.0% in FY 2025 to ₹255,324 crore. The company's EBIT margins, although declining by 30 basis points to 24.3%, remain robust. Additionally, the growth in certain segments such as Communication, Media and Technology (16.5% YoY) and Manufacturing (7.1% YoY) is a positive indicator. The bull case assumes that TCS will continue to benefit from its diversified portfolio, strong client relationships, and ability to adapt to changing market dynamics, leading to revenue growth of 7-8% in the next fiscal year.

On the other hand, the bear case is centered around the potential headwinds from macroeconomic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and fiscal constraints. The company's constant currency revenue growth of 4.2% in FY 2025, which excludes the positive impact of currency movements, is a concern. Furthermore, the decline in segment margins in certain industries, such as Communication, Media and Technology (from 27.7% to 20.9%), may indicate increasing competition and pricing pressure. The bear case assumes that these challenges will persist, leading to a decline in revenue growth to 3-4% in the next fiscal year. Our base case scenario, however, assumes a moderate growth of 5-6% in revenue, driven by the company's ability to navigate the challenges and capitalize on opportunities in the digital transformation space, with EBIT margins remaining stable at around 24%.

eval_context.content: Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 79 Management Discussion and Analysis Overview of the Industry The year 2024 began with signs of improved economic activity across major regions. The world GDP grew at a steady rate of 3.3%1. Despite divergent growth patterns across regions and sectors, the global technology landscape demonstrated unexpected stability. However, in recent weeks, the global outlook has turned negative, as governments worldwide adjust their policy priorities, leading to unprecedented levels of uncertainty. The rapid escalation of trade tensions and extremely high policy uncertainty are anticipated to significantly impact global economic activity. Projections indicate that global growth will decline to 2.8% in 2025 and 3% in 20261. Amid these ongoing macroeconomic challenges, new discretionary projects requiring technology investments will face increased scrutiny and require stronger justifications for return on investment. In 2025, enterprises will be accelerating adoption of AI into their digital core, to address technical debt and modernize legacy systems. This will require efforts in cloud migration, updating infrastructure frameworks and developing a strong data foundation. Enterprises also face a complex risk landscape with cybersecurity threats and geopolitical tensions, making them prime targets for cybercriminals due to their valuable intellectual property and customer data. Enterprises will continue to strengthen their cybersecurity management processes, leading to continued investments in security consulting services2. TCS’ Business An Overview TCS is an IT services, consulting and business solutions organization partnering with many of the world’s largest businesses in their transformational journeys for the last 57 years. The Company leverages all these capabilities and deep contextual knowledge of its customers’ businesses to create bespoke, high quality, and impactful solutions designed to achieve differentiated business outcomes. These solutions are delivered through its operating model which enables a highly distributed, Location Independent Agile™ delivery. TCS considers industry verticals as its primary go-to-market business segments. The five key vertical clusters are: Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI), Communication, Media and Technology (CMT), Consumer Business, Life Sciences and Healthcare, Manufacturing and Others such as Energy, Resources and Utilities, Public Services and Products.

eval_context.content: Customer Stories A global transportation and logistics leader, serving customers in over 200 countries with services like express delivery, freight forwarding, and logistics solutions, has been facing increasing issues with porch piracy and fraud, leading to customer dissatisfaction. In 2023, the Chamber of Commerce reported approximately 44 million packages lost or stolen, amounting to US$5 billion worth of goods lost. The logistics provider sought a solution to assess risks and enhance the security of parcel delivery. It leveraged its partnership with TCS to implement an AI-powered solution that used advanced analytics and petabytes of existing data to provide actionable insights i.e. a ‘Confidence score’ that predicts shipping risks at an address-level and allows shippers to reroute high-risk packages to the logistics provider's stores or access points, preventing loss and theft. This solution enabled merchants and businesses to make smarter, safer shipping decisions even before labels are printed. Additionally, it opened up a new revenue stream for the logistics provider. The solution has a potential to save US$ 500 million annually in the industry. A leading Global Airline had an AI vision – to enable their business users to make intelligent decisions by self-servicing their data needs. However, it’s IT landscape had multiple data platforms, impacting the speed of decision making and the time-to-market, not to mention the high maintenance and licensing costs. The airline turned to its partner of three decades, TCS, to bring all functions under a unified architecture that is easy-to-manage and capable of enabling self-service analytics features. The modernization provided a business glossary for AI to understand and make meaning out of the data, enabling the business users to “talk-to-data” in natural language to derive insights at a faster pace – driving significantly faster decision making with self-service analytics. TCS delivered a highly customized No-Code data platform that replaced proprietary data tools without losing the extensive features, making information readily available and easy to use even by non-technical business users across Marketing, Customer Loyalty, Operations, Engineering, Revenue Management, and other business divisions. Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 92 Internal Financial Control Systems and their Adequacy TCS has aligned its systems of internal financial control in line with the globally accepted risk-based framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations (COSO) of the Treadway Commission. This framework of internal financial controls meets the requirement of the Companies Act, 2013. The Internal Control – Integrated Framework (the 2013 framework) is intended to increase transparency and accountability in an organization’s process of designing and implementing a system of internal control. The framework requires a company to identify and analyze risks and manage appropriate responses. The Company has successfully laid down the framework and ensured its effectiveness. TCS’ internal controls are commensurate with its size and the nature of its operations. These have been designed to provide reasonable assurance with regard to recording and providing reliable financial and operational information, complying with applicable statutes, safeguarding assets from unauthorized use, executing transactions with proper authorization and ensuring compliance with corporate policies. TCS has a well- defined delegation of power with authority limits commensurate with the responsibilities for approving engagements with all stakeholders that commit organizational resources and results in creation of assets and liabilities, income and expenditure. TCS employs an advanced Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system that connects all parts of the organization, to record data for accounting, consolidation and management information purposes. It has continued its efforts to align all its processes and controls with global best practices. TCS management assessed the effectiveness of the Company’s internal control over financial reporting [as defined in Regulation 17 of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015] as of March 31, 2025.
